captured: Probe 1: a LOCAL agent (tools: [], temporary SQLite store, scratch cwd) sent three prompts (a ~6k-token reference list, then two short questions). The streamed turn-ended usage of each run was recorded (localTurnEnded), and agent.getUsage() was called after every run, at the end, and through the static Agent.getUsage(agentId). Every call answered 403 feature_unavailable (localGetUsageFailure).

Probe 2: one no-repo CLOUD agent (cloud: { repos: [] }) REUSED for two sends. Unfiltered agent.getUsage() was read right after each run and five more times over about 20 s (cloudReusedAgent). The agent was deleted afterwards (Agent.delete, then Agent.get answered 404 agent_not_found).

Probe 3 (cloudProductionShape): twice, a FRESH no-repo cloud agent with one prompt, then agent.getUsage({ runId }) right after run.wait() and once more about 5 s later, which is what production does. Each agent was deleted afterwards (Agent.delete, then Agent.get answered 404 agent_not_found).
Agent ids, run ids and usage ids are replaced by labels. No key is recorded.
documented: https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript#agentgetusage (local usage is enabled per account; 403 feature_unavailable until then)
https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#get-agent-usage (documentedExamples.getAgentUsage; getUsage() passes these rows through with runs[].id renamed runId)

https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/admin-api#get-usage-events-data (documentedExamples.adminFilteredUsageEvents; the Get Agent Usage page says its token usage 'matches the tokenUsage reported by' that endpoint)
notes: Production reads getUsage({ runId }) once per finished cloud turn on a FRESH agent: cloudProductionShape is that read. The reused-agent capture (cloudReusedAgent) read unfiltered, so its row shapes, including the all-zero row, are not what production is known to see.

No captured cloud row has cacheReadTokens above inputTokens (12,565 vs 6,560; 21,301 vs 13,120; 7,966 vs 6,560; 13,334 vs 1,184). That the four counts are additive buckets (cache reads can exceed input, totalTokens is their sum) is documented, not captured.
No local getUsage row was ever observed: the capturing account got 403. The SDK documents local entries only as per-turn groups keyed by usage UUID, so the plugin never reads local usage.
Raw local turn-ended usage is a different source: inputTokens is the full prompt and the cache counts partition it.

localGetUsageFailure.message: [feature_unavailable] This feature is not available for your account

observations: afterRun2 was identical on the immediate read and on five further reads over about 20 s: the earlier run's row had grown while the run that had just finished still read as all zeros.
Rows came back in send order (oldest first); the documented example lists them newest first, so run order is not a contract.

cloudProductionShape.description: What production does for a cloud turn: a FRESH no-repo cloud agent (composer-2-5), ONE short prompt ('Do not use any tools. Reply with exactly: OK'), await run.wait() (status finished), then agent.getUsage({ runId }) with that run's run- id right away, and once more about 5 s later. Each agent was deleted afterwards (Agent.delete, then Agent.get answered 404 agent_not_found).
observations: Both immediate reads returned the run's row with recorded (non-zero) counts, and the retry about 5 s later returned the identical row.
A single run had one row, keyed by the run id agent.send() returned. Its counts were about 8k to 13k input and about 1k output for a one-word answer; what they cover is not established.
The reads took 0.8 s to 2.9 s against the plugin's 5 s cap.
No row has cacheReadTokens above inputTokens, so these captures do not show additivity either.

getAgentUsage.source: https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#get-agent-usage (response of GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage; the SDK renames runs[].id to runId)
getAgentUsage.totalTokensDefinition: Sum of the four token counts above.
